decisions.justification: The first question offered reject-all, skip, or choose-unused-name policies, and the user selected “Reject the entire plan before renaming anything, and report every collision.”
The user selected both preflight rejection before any rename and best-effort reverse rollback after an unexpected application failure.
The session never asked whether files already matching the generated naming scheme should be excluded from the input set.
The planned-source-overlap question explicitly asked whether an occupied destination may be used when its occupant is scheduled to move, and the user chose to treat it as a collision.
The planned-source-overlap option explicitly identified accidental reruns and the user chose the policy that rejects them.
No question, repository resolution, or volunteered answer addressed case-only renames on case-insensitive filesystems.
The user was asked about collision-report completeness, rejected-run output streams, and runtime/rollback error reporting, choosing complete stderr diagnostics and failure.
The agent asked whether rejected plans should print proposed rename lines, and the user chose empty stdout rather than relying on proposed-plan output.

mustPreserveKept: user-facing output on stdout and diagnostics on stderr

notes: The session clearly declared a bounded path, used repository-specific evidence, avoided forbidden questions, and implemented the user’s selected collision, locking, rollback, and reporting behavior. It missed the explicit self-inclusion and case-insensitive-filesystem decisions, and best-effort rollback plus validation/application races do not strictly guarantee either acceptance requirement.
